message_variants.message: Tight Mayoral Race Focuses on the Economy. By Anne Davis / The Morning Journal. PATTERSON – In a few weeks, Patterson citizens will go to the polls to choose between two candidates, Gary Rogers and Jack Tucker, who are vying for the seat of retiring Mayor Timothy Marsh. As Election Day draws near, each candidate has turned his focus to what has become the biggest issue in this race: the local economy. Both candidates are long-time residents of Patterson but bring very different credentials to the race. Gary Rogers, 52, is a familiar face in local politics, serving two terms on both the local school board and three terms on the city council. Jack Tucker, 53, is a businessman who has never held elected office but has been active in several community organizations. Throughout his campaign, Jack Tucker has faced harsh questioning about his lack of time in City Hall. Critics have lambasted him for having no political experience, while supporters have made much of the fresh perspective he brings. The two candidates have their own takes on whether experience matters. By pointing out his opponent's shortcomings, Gary Rogers has emphasized that the job of Mayor should not be entrusted to someone without experience. In contrast, Jack Tucker has touted his outsider status, emphasizing the costs associated with entrusting the job of Mayor to someone who has failed to bring about change. And what do local voters think? Both campaigns have been hard at work trying to gauge the pulse of the city. The sentiment appears to be mixed, with recent polls showing the candidates in a dead heat. Some citizens like Jack Tucker's new perspective, while others appreciate Rogers' experience, and still others remain undecided. Cherie Gilbert, 34, says, 'I plan on voting for Gary Rogers. I have been watching the campaign, and I like his ideas.' Rhonda Brady, 29, disagrees. She says, 'I'm all for Jack Tucker. I think he will do a lot of good things for this city.' Both candidates have been holding town hall meetings, attending campaign rallies, and working hard to court voters across the city. Their campaign efforts are sure to pick up as Election Day nears. The election will be held on November 2, 2010. Response display order: Definitely Jack, Probably Jack, Probably Gary, Definitely Gary.

Tight Mayoral Race Focuses on Inexperience. By Anne Davis / The Morning Journal. PATTERSON – In a few weeks, Patterson citizens will go to the polls to choose between two candidates, Gary Rogers and Jack Tucker, who are vying for the seat of retiring Mayor Timothy Marsh. As Election Day draws near, each candidate has turned his focus to what has become the biggest issue in this race: the local economy. Jack Tucker, 53, is a businessman who has never held elected office but has been active in several community organizations. Throughout his campaign, Jack Tucker has faced harsh questioning about his lack of time in City Hall. Critics have lambasted him for having no political experience, while supporters have made much of the fresh perspective he brings. By pointing out his opponent's shortcomings, Gary Rogers has emphasized the risks associated with entrusting the job of Mayor to someone without experience. 'To grow our economy, you have to be able to navigate the political system. This city needs a mayor who knows how local politics works, who has been involved for a while, and who has shown he can get things done. When it comes time for the big game, do you go with the proven veteran or the rookie? A vote for Jack Tucker is too risky: he hasn't been tested in office, you don't know what he stands for, or what he'll be able to accomplish.' And what do local voters think? The sentiment appears to be mixed, with recent polls showing the candidates in a dead heat. Cherie Gilbert, 34, says, 'I plan on voting for Jack Tucker. His energy and new ideas are just what we need to get back on our feet.' Rhonda Brady, 29, disagrees. She says, 'Switching to Jack Tucker is too risky. He's unpredictable and has no record. Gary Rogers has experience, he's a known quantity, and I don't like the idea of trusting the city in the hands of a newcomer.' The election will be held on November 2, 2010. Response display order: Definitely Jack, Probably Jack, Probably Gary, Definitely Gary.

PATTERSON – In a few weeks, Patterson citizens will go to the polls to choose between two candidates, Gary Rogers and Jack Tucker, who are vying for the seat of retiring Mayor Timothy Marsh. Throughout his campaign, Jack Tucker has faced harsh questioning about his lack of time in City Hall. Critics have lambasted him for having no political experience, while supporters have made much of the fresh perspective he brings. By touting his outsider status, Jack Tucker has emphasized the costs associated with entrusting the job of Mayor to someone who has failed to bring about change. We've already had a chance to see what Gary Rogers would do in office, and electing Gary Rogers would just promise the same old approach and the same tired ideas that obviously aren't working. Staying with Gary Rogers is a sure bet, but it's a bad one. You know what you're getting, but what you're betting on has already proven to be unsuccessful.' And what do local voters think? The sentiment appears to be mixed, with recent polls showing the candidates in a dead heat. Cherie Gilbert, 34, says, 'I plan on voting for Gary Rogers. His experience and leadership skills will get us back on our feet.' Rhonda Brady, 29, disagrees. She says, 'I'll take my chances with Jack Tucker. His new ideas give us a good shot at changing things up. Gary Rogers has been in office and has been ineffective. All he's proven is that he can't get things done.' The election will be held on November 2, 2010. Response display order: Definitely Jack, Probably Jack, Probably Gary, Definitely Gary.
